title: The night the sea came in
premise: The tide comes all the way in, across the Reader's floor, and brings a letter from Thimble, lost at sea and following the light. Wick can't see a boat at sea, so Pip goes down to the dark water to be the keeper's eyes.

scenes.summary: A bottle washes up at the Reader's feet with a letter from someone lost at sea

problem.summary: A bottle with a letter has washed up at the Reader's feet

actions.text: The next night, the lamp burned bright, and a new keeper stood on the gallery. A very small one, in a very big coat.
You came back! Wick, look, they came back!
Hmph. So they did. Evening, whoever you are.
I still dream about flying over the gap on that kite.
Moth's still ever so proud of carrying that thread across.
I keep thinking about that ladder. Right across the gap!
Wick says next time I cross a gap, I'm to bring my own rope.
Can I trim the wick tonight, Wick? Please?
Go on, then. Carefully, mind.
That night, the sea came in further than it ever had. Up the shore, up the rocks, and right across the Reader's floor.
The sea's come right in! And look, something's washed up by your feet!
Can you pass it up to us?
A bottle, with a letter in it! Thank you!
Oh, thank you! But it's the bottle we need. The one that washed up!
But the tide, as tides do, brought the bottle the rest of the way by itself.
A bottle! And there's a letter in it!
Wick, it's a letter! Read it, read it!
Hmm. The light's poor up here tonight. You read it, lad.
'To whoever keeps the light: I'm lost on the water. I can see your light, but the rocks keep turning me back. Please keep shining. Thimble.'

actions.outcome: Thimble's letter came up out of the sea

actions.text: The light brings her as far as the rocks. Past them, someone has to call her in.
I'd go. But I couldn't see a paper boat if it sailed up my nose.
Somebody's got to be my eyes, lad.
Down to the water? In the dark?
Not on my own, though. You'll come, won't you?
So down went the little fox, a hundred and twelve steps, to the very edge of the sea.

scenes.summary: Pip's light is too low for Thimble to see from the sea

problem.summary: Pip's lantern is too low for Thimble to see past the rocks

actions.text: At the water's edge, the dark was very big, and the sea was very loud.
There! A little paper boat, going round and round...
Thimble! Over here! Thimble!
But the sea was loud, and the lantern was low, and the little boat went round again.
She can't see me. My light's too low down here.
Is there anything that could get my light up high, where the whole sea can see it?
A kite! Up you go, little light!
Up, up, up! Higher than the rocks!
A ladder! I'll stand it on the rocks, and hang my light at the top.
There. Like a little lighthouse!
Oh, that's lovely. But it won't get my light up high.
Something that flies, maybe? Or something to climb?
Now, if there's one thing a moth knows, it's how to get close to a light.
Moth! Where are you taking my... oh!
Oh, Moth. You clever, clever moth.
Far out on the water, the little boat stopped going round. And turned. And came, slowly, toward the light.
It's very dark down here without my light. But she can see it. That's what matters.
I'm still a little bit scared. Is that all right?
It was. Being a little bit scared is mostly what brave is made of.

actions.outcome: the light went up high, and Thimble turned for home

actions.text: Come on, Moth. She'll come in at the landing.

scenes.summary: Thimble's paper boat is sinking on the rocks below the landing

problem.summary: Thimble's paper boat is sinking on the rocks below the landing

actions.text: The little boat came in out of the dark, right up to the rocks. And there it stuck.
Ahoy! Ahoy, the light!
Thimble? Are you Thimble?
Thimble, from the sewing basket! But my boat's gone soft. Paper boats aren't made for the whole sea.
She's stuck on the rocks! Have you got anything that could bring her in?
That thread! That's my grandmother's thread, from the basket!
Moth, take the end out to her! Hold on tight, Thimble!

actions.outcome: pulled in on her grandmother's thread

actions.text: Hold still, Thimble. And catch!
Steady as she goes! Steady as she goes!
A ladder! Across to the rock, like a bridge!
Mind the gaps between the rungs. Mind the gaps...

actions.outcome: came across a ladder laid like a bridge

actions.text: Grab the tail, Thimble! The wind'll do the rest!
I'm flying! A sailor, flying!

actions.outcome: flew in on a kite tail

actions.text: That won't reach her, I don't think.
Something long, maybe? Something she can hold on to?
And then the sea, which had been so cross all night, gave one last great heave...
...and set the little mouse down on the steps, as gently as anything.

actions.outcome: the sea itself set her down on the steps

actions.text: Land! Real, dry, stay-where-it-is land!
Brr. I'm wet right through to my whiskers.
Here, get in my coat. It's far too big for me anyway.
Pip? I could hear you all the way from the top.
Wick! She's here! The light brought her home!
Hmph. A mouse in a paper boat. Across the whole sea.
Welcome home, little one. Every lost thing that comes home goes in the log.
You write her in, lad. You were my eyes tonight.
Me? In the keeper's log?
'Thimble, from the sewing basket. Came home by the light.'
And the sea, its work done, slipped quietly back out past the edge of the table.
Is that the Reader? The one who reaches down from the sky?
That's them. They came all the way down with me.
Much obliged, Reader. Truly.
Same time tomorrow, keeper?
Same time tomorrow.
And whatever the Reader gave that night, the book kept safe, for another time.
But the nights were growing longer, and the old keeper's eyes were growing dimmer. And the longest night of all was on its way.
Out on the dark water, a paper boat bobbed, and waited, and hoped.
The sea breathed in, and the sea breathed out.
Up at the top of the lighthouse, the great lamp went round, and round.
